name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,796

entries.clue: Groovy district in an English county? (7)

blocks.note: a rut is a groove, so 'groovy' is read as 'rut'
a district or tract of land

annotation.surface: Someone looking for a hip, happening neighbourhood somewhere in provincial England.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' means trendy on the surface, but here it describes land full of grooves; the question mark flags the liberty. Rutland is England's smallest county.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Rutland is one English county, the smallest of them, in the East Midlands.

entries.clue: Get the next round in? (6)

blocks.note: read as the pub call to buy the next set of drinks for the group
meant as a round of ammunition, loaded into the gun's chamber

annotation.surface: A pub drinker being told it is their turn to buy drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'round' in a pub is a set of drinks bought for the group; here it is a round of ammunition put into a gun.
annotation.definitionFit: To reload a gun is to put the next round of ammunition into it.

entries.clue: See 20
Arrogance shown in an RC feast? (10)

blocks.note: presumption, taking too much upon oneself
the Roman Catholic feast of Mary taken up into heaven, 15 August

annotation.surface: A haughty display at a Roman Catholic celebration.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shown in' makes the arrogance sound like behaviour at the feast; in fact the feast and the arrogance share one word, and the question mark admits the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Assumption can mean presumptuous arrogance, and the Assumption is a Roman Catholic feast day.

entries.clue: Remove trousers — bad egg to miss a good thrashing (5)

indicatorNotes.to miss: the G is left out of the fodder
indicatorNotes.thrashing: beating the letters about rearranges them

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
G is the standard abbreviation for good; one G goes, leaving BADEG

annotation.surface: A schoolboy prank: a rotter debagged and then given a beating.
annotation.walkthrough: To debag is old British schoolboy slang for pulling someone's trousers off as a prank.
annotation.definitionFit: Debag means to strip someone of their trousers, bags being slang for trousers.

entries.clue: Adult rabbit going outside to get drink (7)

indicatorNotes.going outside: LOP goes round the outside of COP

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a lop is a breed of rabbit with drooping ears
to cop is slang for to get or catch

annotation.surface: A grown-up rabbit hopping out of the burrow in search of refreshment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To get' looks like a link to the definition, but 'get' is COP and it sits inside the rabbit.
annotation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet, fizzy alcoholic drink.

entries.clue: Shock when pair climbing spotted mount (9)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down entry, going up means read from the bottom

blocks.note: to appal is to shock
as in 'as I left' = 'when I left'
in cricket a pair is two ducks, scores of 0 in both innings

annotation.surface: Horror at a couple scrambling up onto a spotted horse.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'pair' is the cricket term for being out for nought in both innings, hence two Os.
annotation.definitionFit: The Appaloosa is an American horse breed with a spotted coat.

entries.clue: I'm surprised by king in Irish city (4)

blocks.note: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise
K is king in chess notation

annotation.surface: Someone amazed to meet a monarch in an Irish city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is informal British English for 'wow!'.
annotation.definitionFit: Cork is the second city of the Republic of Ireland.

entries.clue: Margaret covering one with Nancy's black dressing-gown (8)

indicatorNotes.covering: to cover something is to lie over it on all sides, so PEG wraps round I
indicatorNotes.Nancy's: Nancy is a French city, so its word for black is French

blocks.note: Peg is a pet form of Margaret
Roman numeral one
French for black

annotation.surface: Margaret throwing a black gown over a friend called Nancy.
annotation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name beside Margaret, but it is the city in north-east France.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is borrowed from French, where it first meant a cape worn while combing the hair.

entries.clue: In crowd Treebeard for one holds out (8)

blocks.note: a press is a crowd or throng
Treebeard is an Ent, a tree-giant in The Lord of the Rings

annotation.surface: In a crowd, a Tolkien character holds out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For one' marks Treebeard as an example of a class: he is one of the Ents.
annotation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out for someone to take.

entries.clue: Inspector's wife visiting stormy isle (5)

indicatorNotes.visiting: W goes inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.stormy: a storm tosses the letters of ISLE about

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for wife
taken letter for letter

annotation.surface: A detective's wife paying a visit to a wild, windswept island.
annotation.walkthrough: Inspector Lewis is a British TV detective, formerly Morse's sergeant. The surface also suggests Lewis the Hebridean isle.
annotation.definitionFit: Lewis is the Oxford detective inspector of the ITV series Lewis.

entries.clue: Single portion fills in snack in two sections (9)

indicatorNotes.fills: I and PART fill the middle of BITE

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a part is a portion
a bite is a snack

annotation.surface: A single helping stuffed into a snack that is split into two halves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In two sections' looks like part of the snack's description, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Bipartite means having or divided into two parts.

entries.clue: Disease in which mercy a goal potentially (10)

indicatorNotes.potentially: the letters could potentially become another word

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

annotation.surface: A disease whose cure might one day be a merciful aim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' means the letters are only a possible version of something else, which is why they get rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Acromegaly is a hormonal disease causing enlargement of the hands, feet and face.

entries.clue: Kay previously called for joint (4)

blocks.note: a sound: 'kay' is how the letter K is said, so the name stands for the letter
née introduces a woman's former surname

annotation.surface: A woman named Kay who used to go by another name.
annotation.walkthrough: Kay looks like a woman's name, fitting with née, but it stands for the letter K.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the knee is one joint of many in the body.

entries.clue: Austere existence is seen among cats at war with mice (10)

indicatorNotes.among: IS is placed among the other letters
indicatorNotes.at war: the letters of cats and mice fight and scatter

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter

annotation.surface: A spartan life is the lot of cats forever battling mice.
annotation.walkthrough: The first 'is' is a link word; the second one is the IS that goes inside the jumbled cats and mice.
annotation.definitionFit: Asceticism is a life of strict self-denial.

entries.clue: Singer one seen in uproarious 20 2: we must leave! (6,5)

indicatorNotes.seen in: something seen in a show appears within it, so I is placed within the other letters
indicatorNotes.uproarious: an uproar throws the letters into disorder
indicatorNotes.must leave: the letters W and E are removed

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
the answer to 20/2
taken letter for letter, and removed

annotation.surface: A pop star appearing in a riotous episode of Fawlty Towers and being told to get out.
annotation.walkthrough: Add I to FAWLTY TOWERS, take away one W and the E, and rearrange the remaining eleven letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Taylor Swift is one singer, the American pop star.

entries.clue: Husband in jeopardy back in times past finds pig (9)

indicatorNotes.in: one group of letters goes inside another
indicatorNotes.back: to go back is to go the way you came, so the letters are written from the far end

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for husband
to be in jeopardy is to be at risk
'days of yore' are times past

annotation.surface: A husband in danger in olden days turns up a pig.
annotation.walkthrough: The order matters: the husband goes into the jeopardy first, then that whole word turns back, then it lands inside the times past. A Yorkshire is a pig breed, not only a county.
annotation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire, or Large White, is a breed of domestic pig.

entries.clue: French pop excessive American consumes for entertainment (8)

indicatorNotes.consumes: to consume is to eat, and what is eaten ends up inside, so OTT A holds PERE
indicatorNotes.French: the word for pop is taken in French

blocks.note: père is French for father, and pop is a word for father
OTT is short for over the top
standard abbreviation for American

annotation.surface: Over-the-top French pop music eaten up by an American audience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests music, fitting the entertainment theme, but it means dad, so French pop is PERE.
annotation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera, a form of entertainment.

entries.clue: Lock spring breaks giving uninvited access? (8)

indicatorNotes.breaks: what breaks something splits it open and sits in the gap, so SPA goes inside TRESS

blocks.note: a lock or tress of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

annotation.surface: A lock whose spring gives way, letting a burglar in.
annotation.walkthrough: Lock and spring suggest a mechanism being forced, but a lock is hair and a spring is water.
annotation.definitionFit: Trespass is entering land or property without permission.

entries.clue: Endlessly dangerous Romeo up for fun indoors (7,4)

indicatorNotes.Endlessly: the last letter of PARLOUS is dropped

blocks.note: parlous means dangerous; without its end it is PARLOU
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to be game is to be up for something

annotation.surface: A reckless lover keen on some fun at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dangerous' is parlous, an old word for perilous; 'up for' reads as a phrase about the Romeo but gives GAME.
annotation.definitionFit: A parlour game is a word or guessing game played indoors.

entries.clue: Setter barking shows way (6)

indicatorNotes.barking: British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

annotation.surface: A setter dog barking to show someone the way.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has a setter dog barking; 'barking' is British slang for mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A street is a way, as in road names like Watling Way.

entries.clue: Drag queen's chasing buggy we hear in sitcom (6,6)

indicatorNotes.we hear: FAULTY is spelt as it sounds

blocks.note: buggy software is faulty
to drag or tow
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
the S of queen's

annotation.surface: A drag queen pursuing a pushchair on the set of a comedy show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' reads as one phrase but splits in two; a buggy is British for a pushchair, and in computing a buggy program is faulty.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Fawlty Towers is the 1970s BBC sitcom set in a hotel, starring John Cleese.

entries.clue: Prickly shrub took an upward course (4)

blocks.note: the thorny garden flower bush
the past tense of rise

annotation.surface: A thorny bush climbing ever higher.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a climbing rose, so the two halves seem to describe one plant; one is a noun, the other a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A rose is a thorny shrub, and rose is the past tense of rise.

entries.clue: Plant at least three detectives in Vauxhall? (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the detectives go inside the car

blocks.note: the Astra is a Vauxhall car model
a PI (private investigator) plus DIS (detective inspectors), so three or more

annotation.surface: Police planting a team of detectives inside a car.
annotation.walkthrough: Vauxhall is a British car maker and the Astra one of its models; 'at least three' counts one PI plus two or more DIs.
annotation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy house plant.

entries.clue: Map detail — it describes three main points (5)

indicatorNotes.describes: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so IT goes round NSE

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
north, south and east are cardinal points of the compass

annotation.surface: A cartographer explaining what a small map feature shows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Describes' is used in its geometry sense, to draw a line round something.
annotation.definitionFit: An inset is a small map set within a larger one, showing detail.

entries.clue: Wrongdoer renouncing evil without real worth (4)

indicatorNotes.renouncing: to renounce something is to give it up, so the wrongdoer gives up the letters for evil

blocks.note: a villain is a wrongdoer
ill means evil or harm

annotation.surface: A criminal going straight but still worthless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without real worth' looks like more description of the reformed wrongdoer, but it is the definition, as in 'in vain'.
annotation.definitionFit: Vain means futile, lacking any real value or effect.

entries.clue: Office workers' duck croaks having swallowed article (3,6)

indicatorNotes.having swallowed: what is swallowed ends up inside, so the article sits within TEAL DIES

blocks.note: a teal is a small duck
the indefinite article
to croak is slang for to die

annotation.surface: A duck choking to death on something it ate.
annotation.walkthrough: Tea ladies once brought tea round British offices on a trolley. 'Croaks' suggests frog noise but means dies.
annotation.definitionFit: Tea ladies were women employed to serve tea to office staff.

entries.clue: Principle that is absorbing Democrat completely? Almost! (5)

indicatorNotes.absorbing: to absorb is to soak something up and hold it within, so IE holds D
indicatorNotes.Almost: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: i.e. is Latin id est, that is
standard abbreviation
ALL, as in all over, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A principle that nearly wins a Democrat over completely.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Almost!' look like a comment on the Democrat, but 'Almost' is an instruction acting on 'completely'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one's ideals are the principles one holds.

entries.clue: Dope dealer in seconds confessed in A&E (7)

indicatorNotes.in: S and SANG go inside A and E

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
standard abbreviation for seconds
to sing is slang for to confess to the police

annotation.surface: A drug dealer blurting out a confession while in hospital casualty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' here is inside information, not drugs: Julian Assange of WikiLeaks dealt in leaked secrets. A&E is British hospital casualty.
annotation.definitionFit: Julian Assange published leaked secret information, dope in the slang sense.

entries.clue: Grass and tree riddled with insects (7)

blocks.note: the ti is a palm-like tree of the Pacific
mothy means full of moths

annotation.surface: A lawn and a tree infested with bugs.
annotation.walkthrough: The ti is a tree of Polynesia and Australasia, handy for setters; mothy means infested with moths.
annotation.definitionFit: Timothy is a meadow grass grown for hay.
